title: Fish Amritsari
description: Fish Amritsari is a classic Punjabi delicacy from Amritsar, featuring tender white fish coated in a crisp, spiced gram flour batter. Aromatic ajwain, coriander, garam masala, and mustard oil give the dish its signature Punjabi flavor and irresistible crunch.

ingredients.title: For the Marinade
items: Firm white fish fillets – 500 g, such as basa, cod, sole, or tilapia, cut into 2–3 inch pieces
Red chili powder – 1 tsp, adjust to taste

ingredients.title: For the Coating
items: Water – 2–3 tbsp, or as required for a thick batter

ingredients.title: For Frying
items: Mustard oil or refined oil – enough for deep frying

ingredients.title: For Serving
items: Onion rings – soaked in cold water for crunch

instruction.title: Step 1 – First Marinade
steps: Pat the fish pieces dry with kitchen paper.
Mix ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, lemon juice, and salt in a bowl.
Coat the fish pieces evenly with the marinade.
Cover and let the fish rest for 15 minutes.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Preparing the Spiced Coating
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine gram flour, cornflour, coriander powder, garam masala, crushed ajwain, and baking soda.
Add just enough water to form a thick batter that clings to the fish.
Add the pre-marinated fish and toss until each piece is evenly coated.
Let the coated fish rest for another 10 minutes so the flavors penetrate.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Frying the Fish
steps: Heat mustard oil to 180°C. Test the temperature by dropping a little batter into the oil; it should rise immediately and sizzle.
Fry the fish in small batches to avoid overcrowding the pan.
Turn the pieces once and fry for about 3–4 minutes per batch, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain the fried fish on paper towels.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Plating and Serving
steps: Arrange the hot fish on a warm serving platter.
Add crisp onion rings and lemon wedges.
Sprinkle with freshly chopped coriander leaves.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings, and lemon wedges.
Garnish with fresh coriander for a bright, aromatic finish.
For fine-dining presentation, serve on a banana leaf over a stone platter with chutney in a small katori.

chefTips: Ajwain is essential for the signature Fish Amritsari aroma and helps balance the richness of the fried fish.
For extra restaurant-style crispness, double-fry the fish: first at 160°C until almost cooked, rest for 1 minute, then fry again at 190°C for 30–40 seconds.
Mustard oil adds authentic Punjabi depth; heat it until smoking and allow it to cool slightly before frying to mellow its pungency.
Keep the batter thick enough to cling to the fish and create a crisp, even coating.
Fry in small batches so the oil temperature stays high and the coating remains crisp.
